# Resource: stripe_treasury_financial_account

A Treasury financial account that holds money on a connected account and that Issuing cards draw on. Treasury runs on a platform's connected accounts, so manage financial accounts through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is a connected account with the `treasury` capability active. `features` requests features when the account is created; `active_features`, `pending_features` and `restricted_features` say how Stripe answered. A plan that changes `features` afterwards fails: create a new financial account instead.

~> Stripe can close a financial account, but the provider does not do so yet: `terraform destroy` leaves the financial account open on the connected account and removes it from state. Changing `supported_currencies` replaces it, which leaves the old one open too.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "treasury_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A connected account with the treasury capability active."
}

# Treasury runs on a connected account, so a second provider configuration acts on it.
provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "treasury"
  stripe_account = var.treasury_account
}

resource "stripe_treasury_financial_account" "operating" {
  provider             = stripe.treasury
  supported_currencies = ["usd"]
  features = {
    card_issuing = { requested = true }
  }
  metadata = {
    purpose = "card spending"
  }
}

output "active_features" {
  value = stripe_treasury_financial_account.operating.active_features
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `supported_currencies` - (Required) The currencies the FinancialAccount can hold a balance in. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `features` - (Optional) Encodes whether a FinancialAccount has access to a particular feature. Stripe or the platform can control features via the requested field. See [`features`](#features) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `nickname` - (Optional) The nickname for the FinancialAccount.
* `platform_restrictions` - (Optional) The set of functionalities that the platform can restrict on the FinancialAccount. See [`platform_restrictions`](#platform_restrictions) below.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `active_features` - The array of paths to active Features in the Features hash.
* `balance` - Balance information for the FinancialAccount See [`balance`](#balance) below.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `financial_addresses` - The set of credentials that resolve to a FinancialAccount. See [`financial_addresses`](#financial_addresses) below.
* `is_default` -
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `pending_features` - The array of paths to pending Features in the Features hash.
* `restricted_features` - The array of paths to restricted Features in the Features hash.
* `status` - Status of this FinancialAccount. Possible values: `closed`, `open`.
* `status_details` - See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.

<a id="balance"></a>
### `balance`

The `balance` attribute supports:

* `cash` - Funds the user can spend right now.
* `inbound_pending` - Funds not spendable yet, but will become available at a later time.
* `outbound_pending` - Funds in the account, but not spendable because they are being held for pending outbound flows.

<a id="financial_addresses"></a>
### `financial_addresses`

The `financial_addresses` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `aba` - ABA Records contain U.S. bank account details per the ABA format. See [`financial_addresses.aba`](#financial_addresses.aba) below.
* `supported_networks` - The list of networks that the address supports
* `type` - The type of financial address Possible values: `aba`.

<a id="financial_addresses.aba"></a>
### `financial_addresses.aba`

The `financial_addresses.aba` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_name` - The name of the person or business that owns the bank account.
* `account_number` - (Sensitive) The account number.
* `account_number_last4` - The last four characters of the account number.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank.
* `routing_number` - Routing number for the account.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `closed` - Details related to the closure of this FinancialAccount See [`status_details.closed`](#status_details.closed) below.

<a id="status_details.closed"></a>
### `status_details.closed`

The `status_details.closed` attribute supports:

* `reasons` - The array that contains reasons for a FinancialAccount closure.

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

Run the import where the resource's `provider` acts on the connected account that holds it.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a treasury financial account using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_financial_account.operating
  id = "fa_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixUqlIQr8T"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_treasury_financial_account.operating
  identity = {
    id = "fa_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixUqlIQr8T"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the treasury financial account.

Using `terraform import`, import a treasury financial account using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_treasury_financial_account.operating fa_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixUqlIQr8T
```

~> Stripe does not return which features were requested, so an imported financial account has no `features` in state. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [features] }` to a configuration that sets it, because a plan that changes `features` fails.
